analysis.title: European Equity Daily - 18th November
key_insights: Voestalpine (VOE AV) upgraded to Buy from Hold with a EUR48 PT. Shares have underperformed EU steel peers by 27-50% YTD and the SXPP by 17%, and trade on 3.7x EV/EBITDA versus a 10-year average of 5.1x. FY27-28 earnings expectations were reset lower after the 2Q guidance cut.
For earnings leverage to higher steel prices next year, Jefferies still prefers SZG and MT over Voestalpine.

FLSmidth (FLS DC, Buy, PT DKK700) CMD: organic revenue growth targets look potentially conservative. The working capital-to-sales ratio should peak in 2Q27F, buybacks will continue beyond the current programme, and no detail was given on the CFO's recent departure.

SSE 1H26/27: adjusted EPS 66.5p, within the 64-68p range flagged in October. Transmission operating profit doubled to GBP584m and Thermal turned to GBP78m from a GBP22m loss. FY27 EPS guidance of 168-193p and 2030 EPS of 225-250p are unchanged. The interim dividend rose 7% to 22.9p.
Jet2 1H was robust with record passengers and revenues. At current jet fuel rates, consensus FY27E/FY28E EBIT could fall 12%/22% to c.GBP220m/c.GBP295m.
Hill & Smith is acquiring Southwest Galvanizing for US$77m. Jefferies expects the deal to be low-single-digit accretive to FY27F EPS.
SQM 3Q26 adjusted EBITDA was US$1.03bn, down 21% QoQ and c5% below FactSet consensus. Management points to a weaker 4Q26.

dormakaba set new FY28/29 targets: IFRS operating margin of c.14% (about 400bps above FY25/26), 3-5% organic growth plus 3-5% inorganic growth, and ROCE above 35%. Jefferies expects high-single-digit to low-double-digit upgrades to FY28/29 consensus.

Smiths Group 1Q27 trading update was in line with no change to the FY27 outlook (c4% organic sales growth, c21% EBITA margin). Organic sales were flat in the period and Jefferies stays at Hold with a muted share reaction expected.
British Land H1: underlying profit +7% to GBP166m, EPS +5% to 16.1p. FY27 underlying EPS guidance was raised to 31.0p (+7% YoY). Jefferies rates it Underperform with a PT of 331p.
Corporacion America Airports 3Q26 adjusted EBITDA was US$191m, down 2.2% YoY and c4% below consensus. Argentina EBITDA fell c13% YoY.
Compass Group: Jefferies sees a compelling FY27 setup on accelerating net new wins, margin expansion and renewed buybacks, with shares at c.20x NTM P/E. Buy, PT $40 unchanged.
Fincantieri trades at 5.5x NTM EV/EBITDA, about 2x below its 10-year average. SOTP and DCF both point to c.EUR19 per share.

Dassault Systemes (Underperform, PT EUR19): the CMD set out an AI growth opportunity, but there is a long-standing gap between opportunity and delivered growth and valuation already prices in success.
Sixt (Buy, PT EUR100): guidance was upgraded, European momentum is strong and US share gains continue. It trades at 9.7x 2027 P/E.

Jefferies London Healthcare Conference notes: Roche (Underperform) saw US giredestrant approval at a $22.5k/month list price. AstraZeneca management called its $80bn ambition increasingly credible. Sanofi was pitched as underappreciated in vaccines.
Vinci October traffic: airports -1.4% YoY and roads -6.1% YoY, with high fuel prices and geopolitical tensions weighing.
US: Home Depot 3Q comp sales +2.2%, EBIT margin at the low end of the 2026 guide, and CFO Richard McPhail is replacing CEO Ted Decker.
US: Amer Sports 3Q revenue +24% and adjusted operating margin 16.4% (consensus 21.6% and 14.5%), with a beat and raise. FY26 EPS guidance is $1.32-1.35 and a new $1B buyback was announced.
US: Nike Investor Day framework targets 12-14% operating margin and $3.00-3.50 EPS by FY30-31, with FY27 seen as the trough. Jefferies stays at Buy, PT $60.
US: Viking 3Q missed on low river water levels, a $100M impact versus Jefferies' $60M. FY27 advance bookings are +17%.
US: Nextpower FY30 guidance of $7.5bn revenue and $1.6bn EBITDA was above JEFe/consensus on revenue ($7.0bn/$6.7bn).
US: IDACORP was downgraded to Hold from Buy on valuation. Spire cut FY27 guidance by about 6%.
US credit: total 4Q bankruptcies are projected up 12% Y/Y, while large and medium filings are down 20% Y/Y, which Jefferies reads as stable to improving commercial credit losses.
US healthcare: flu ILI patients in Week 44 were 88,695, up 14% on the week and 94% Y/Y, with positive flu tests up 863% Y/Y and confirmed flu admits up 608% Y/Y.

sector_views.rationale: Jefferies sees its constructive view as intact on long-term rates, ROE versus cost of equity, de-risking of new sales and 2027E capital return yields. Top picks are LNC, EQH and CRBG.

earnings_insights: SSE 1H26/27: adjusted EPS 66.5p (reported, within the 64-68p range flagged in October). Interim dividend 22.9p, up 7% YoY.
British Land H1 (reported): underlying profit GBP166m (+7%), EPS 16.1p (+5%). FY27 underlying EPS guidance raised to 31.0p (+7% YoY).

CAAP 3Q26 (reported): adjusted EBITDA US$191m, c4% below VA/FS consensus and in line with Jefferies' forecast.

Home Depot 3Q (reported): comp sales +2.2% versus a buyside bar of about 2%. EBIT margin is guided to the low end of the 2026 range and EPS to the midpoint.
Viking 3Q (reported): below expectations on a $100M low river water impact versus Jefferies' $60M estimate.
Spire F4Q26 (reported): adjusted EPS of $(0.99) versus JEF estimate of $(1.01). FY26 EPS was $4.02, in line with consensus. FY27 guidance midpoint is $5.15.
Nextpower FY30 guidance: revenue of $7.5bn and EBITDA of $1.6bn versus JEFe/consensus of $7.0bn/$6.7bn on revenue and $1.6bn/$1.5bn on EBITDA.
New Jersey Resources: FY27 guide expected near $3.30 versus the JEFe FY27 estimate of $3.26 (forecast, update due Wednesday).
Unite Group: FY26 adjusted EPS guidance unchanged at 41.5-43.0p.
LuxExperience Q1 (reported): constant-currency revenue +8.5% versus +7.6% in Q4, with adjusted EBITDA positive for a fourth straight quarter.
Max Stock 3Q (reported): same-store sales +11.2%, gross margin +380bps and adjusted EBITDA +45.7%.
Jet2: current jet fuel rates imply consensus FY27E/FY28E EBIT could fall 12%/22% to c.GBP220m/c.GBP295m (Jefferies' estimate).
